source_text: {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι ὃ φής. {ΚΥΡ.} Οἶμαι δὲ ἔγωγε, τὴν ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἀαρὼν θυσίαν καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ παραδηλοῦν ἀστείως τὴν τῶν ἁγίων εἰς Θεὸν καθιέρωσιν. Ἀναδεδειγμένου δὲ λοιπὸν καὶ ἐμφανῆ τὰ καθ' ἑαυτὸν καταστήσαντος τοῦ Ἐμμανουὴλ, δι' οὗ κεκλήμεθα πρὸς ἁγιασμὸν, δεκτοί τε καὶ ἱεροὶ, καὶ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀνατεθείμεθα τῷ Πατρί. Ἐπιτήρει γὰρ ὅτι, διὰ τῶν ἔναγχος εἰρημένων, ἐπεραίνετο μὲν ἐννόμως ἡ τῶν ἱερέων τελείωσις, δι' αὐτοῦ δὲ δὴ πάλιν πολυτρόπως ἡγιασμένων. Κατεκαίετο μὲν γὰρ ὡς μόσχος ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας, ἐθυμιᾶτο δὲ ὡς κριὸς καθηκόντως ὁλοκαυτούμενος, μελειστὶ δὲ ὅλος ὡς ὑπὲρ ἑκάστου καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντων, ἡγίαζε τῷ αἵματι καταχρίων αὐτοὺς, ὡς κριὸς σωτηρίου. Ὀγδόης δὲ ἤδη λοιπὸν ἀναδεδειγμένης ἡμέρας, τοῦτ' ἔστι, καθ' ἣν ἐκφανεστέρα γέγονεν ἡ δόξα Χριστοῦ, κατηργημένου θανάτου, καὶ πεπατημένης φθορᾶς, λοιπὸν ἱερεῖς τε καὶ λαοὶ καρποφοροῦσι Θεῷ, οὐκ ὀθνείοις τιμῶντές τισιν, οὐδὲ τοῖς ἔξωθεν εὐφραίνοντες τὸν τῶν ὅλων Δεσπότην, καθάπερ καὶ ὁ κατὰ σάρκα Ἰσραὴλ, ἀλλὰ ἑαυτοὺς ἀποφαίνοντες εὐώδη θυσίαν. Οἱονεὶ γάρ πως ἐν εἰκόνι τοῖς θύμασι τὰς ἑαυτῶν ἱερουργοῦμεν ψυχὰς, καὶ Θεῷ προσάγομεν, ἀποθνήσκοντες μὲν τῷ κόσμῳ, καὶ τῷ φρονεῖν τὰ σαρκὸς, καὶ παθῶν νέκρωσιν ὑπομένοντες, μόνον δὲ οὐχὶ συσταυρούμενοι τῷ Χριστῷ, ἵνα πρὸς ἁγίαν καὶ ἀμώμητον μεταχωροῦντες ζωὴν, κατὰ τὸ αὐτῷ δοκοῦν πολιτευώμεθα. Τοιοῦτόν τι καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος γράφει Παῦλος· «Πάντοτε τὴν νέκρωσιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι περιφέροντες, ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι ἡμῶν φανερωθῇ.» Καὶ πάλιν· «Εἰ ὑπομένομεν, καὶ συμβασιλεύσομεν·» εἰ συμμορφούμεθα τῷ θανάτῳ καὶ τοῖς παθήμασιν αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, κοινωνοὶ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως καὶ τῆς δόξης ἐσόμεθα. Οὐκοῦν ἔξω μὲν τῆς πύλης ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πέπονθεν ὁ Χριστὸς, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου φωνὴν, ἔξιμεν δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ, τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν αὐτοῦ φέροντες, ἔξω τῆς πύλης, ὡς μοσχάριον ἐν ἴσῳ τρόπῳ σφαζόμενοι, καὶ ὡς κριὸς ὁλοκαυτούμενοι, τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ πολιτείαν εὐωδιάζομεν τῷ Θεῷ· Καὶ ταυτὶ μὲν ὑπὲρ Ἀαρὼν καὶ τῶν σὺν αὐτῷ τε καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὰ θύματα, τὰ δὲ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ, χίμαρος τὸ ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας. Καὶ τίς ὁ λόγος; καίτοι μοσχαρίου προσενηνεγμένου πρὸς ἀποκάθαρσιν ἱερέων. Ἐν ὑπεροχῇ δὲ πάντα τὰ ἱερέων, καὶ θυσίας προσαγωγαὶ, καὶ τὰ εἰς ἀποκάθαρσίν τε καὶ ἁγνισμόν· μείζων δὲ ὡς ἐν μεγέθει σώματος χιμάρου μοσχάριον, τῆς ἐν πράγμασι νοητῆς ὑπεροχῆς μηνύσιον ἐμφαῖνον ἐναργές. Μοσχάριον δὲ καὶ ἀμνὸς εἰς ὁλοκάρπωσιν τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ νηπιότητα τῶν ἐν πίστει καθιερουμένων ὑπαινίττεται· μόσχος δὲ καὶ κριὸς τὸ τληπαθὲς καὶ ἀνδρεῖον, καὶ τὴν ἐν πραότητι καρποφορίαν κατασημαίνουσιν εὖ μάλα καὶ τοῦ μὲν πρώτου τύπος ὁ μόσχος· ὁ δέ γε κριὸς τοῦ δευτέρου. Διάβροχος δὲ τῷ ἐλαίῳ σεμίδαλις τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ ζωῆς τὴν ἐλπίδα λαμπρὰν εὖ μάλα καταδηλοῖ· οὐ γάρ τοι στυγνάζοντας καὶ δεδακρυμένους,
pass_a_gloss: PALL: I understand what you say. CYR: I think the sacrifice for Aaron and for the people elegantly (ἀστείως) indicates (παραδηλόω) the consecration (καθιέρωσις) of the saints to God. Emmanuel (Ἐμμανουήλ) having now been shown forth (ἀναδείκνυμι) and having made manifest (ἐμφανής) the things concerning himself, through whom we have been called (καλέω) to sanctification (ἁγιασμός), acceptable (δεκτός) and sacred (ἱερός), and we have been dedicated (ἀνατίθημι) to the Father unto an odor of sweet smell (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας). Observe (ἐπιτηρέω) that through the things just said the perfecting (τελείωσις) of the priests was being accomplished (περαίνω) lawfully (ἐννόμως), they being sanctified (ἁγιάζω) again through him in many ways (πολυτρόπως). For he was burned (κατακαίω) as a calf (μόσχος) outside the camp (παρεμβολή) for sin; he was made smoke (θυμιάω) as a ram fittingly wholly burnt (ὁλοκαυτόω), and whole limb by limb (μελειστί) as for each and for all; he sanctified by anointing (καταχρίω) them with blood, as a ram of salvation (κριὸς σωτηρίου). The eighth day now having been shown forth, that is, on which the glory (δόξα) of Christ became more manifest, death having been abolished (καταργέω) and corruption (φθορά) trampled (πατέω), priests and peoples (λαοί) bear fruit (καρποφορέω) to God, not honoring with some foreign things (ὀθνεῖος), nor gladdening (εὐφραίνω) the Master (Δεσπότης) of all with external things, as also Israel according to flesh (κατὰ σάρκα), but showing themselves a fragrant (εὐώδης) sacrifice. For as it were somehow in image (εἰκών) by the victims (θῦμα) we sacrifice (ἱερουργέω) our own souls (ψυχή), and bring them (προσάγω) to God, dying (ἀποθνῄσκω) to the world (κόσμος) and to minding the things of flesh (φρονεῖν τὰ σαρκός), and undergoing (ὑπομένω) mortification (νέκρωσις) of passions (πάθος), all but co-crucified (συσταυρόω) with Christ, so that changing over (μεταχωρέω) to holy and blameless (ἀμώμητος) life we may live as citizens (πολιτεύομαι) according to what seems good to him. Such also the inspired (θεσπέσιος) Paul writes: 'Always carrying about the dying (νέκρωσις) of Jesus in the body, so that also the life of Jesus may be manifested (φανερόω) in our body.' And again: 'If we endure, we shall also co-reign (συμβασιλεύω).' If we are conformed (συμμορφόω) to the death and his sufferings (πάθημα), according to what is written, we will be sharers (κοινωνός) of the resurrection and the glory. So outside the gate (πύλη) Christ suffered (πάσχω) for us, according to the voice of blessed Paul; and we ourselves go out (ἔξειμι), bearing his reproach (ὀνειδισμός), outside the gate, slaughtered in equal manner as a young calf (μοσχάριον), and wholly burnt as a ram, we make fragrant (εὐωδιάζω) the citizenship/way of life (πολιτεία) in Christ to God. And these are the victims for Aaron and those with him and from him; those for the people, a male goat (χίμαρος) the one for sin. And what is the reason? although a young calf was offered for purging (ἀποκάθαρσις) of priests. All the things of priests are in pre-eminence (ὑπεροχή), both offerings of sacrifice and things for purging and purification (ἁγνισμός); a young calf is greater in size of body than a goat, displaying a clear indication (μηνύσιον) of the intelligible (νοητός) pre-eminence in realities (πρᾶγμα). Young calf and lamb for whole burnt offering (ὁλοκάρπωσις) hint (ὑπαινίττομαι) at the infancy (νηπιότης) in Christ of those consecrated (καθιερόω) in faith; calf and ram signify (κατασημαίνω) the enduring (τληπαθής) and manly/courageous (ἀνδρεῖος), and the fruit-bearing (καρποφορία) in gentleness (πραότης) very well; and of the first the calf is a type, the ram of the second. Fine flour soaked (διάβροχος) with oil shows (καταδηλόω) the hope (ἐλπίς) of the life in Christ as bright (λαμπρός) very well; for not being gloomy (στυγνάζω) and having wept (δακρύω), [continues in 24].
pass_b_english: Palladius: I understand what you mean.

Cyril: For my part, I think that the sacrifice for Aaron and for the people neatly hints at the consecration of the saints to God. Emmanuel has now been revealed and has made plain all that concerns him; through him we have been called to sanctification, made acceptable and consecrated, and dedicated to the Father for a fragrant aroma. For notice that, through the rites just described, the perfecting of the priests was carried out according to the law, while it was through him, in turn, that they were sanctified in many ways. For he was burned like a calf outside the camp for sin (Leviticus 9:11); he was offered up in smoke like a ram duly burned whole, all of him, limb by limb, as though for each one and for all (Leviticus 9:13); and he sanctified them by anointing them with blood, as the ram of salvation. Now that the eighth day has dawned, that is, the day on which the glory of Christ became more manifest, when death was abolished and corruption trampled down, priests and people alike bear fruit for God. They do not honor him with things foreign to them, nor delight the Master of all with things from outside, as Israel according to the flesh did (1 Corinthians 10:18), but they show themselves to be a fragrant sacrifice. For in a way, as if in the likeness of the victims, we offer up our own souls in sacrifice and bring them to God. We die to the world and to minding the things of the flesh (Romans 8:5), we endure the putting to death of the passions, and we are all but crucified with Christ (Galatians 2:19–20), so that, passing over to a holy and blameless life, we may live as he wills. The inspired Paul, too, writes something of this kind: ‘Always carrying about in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our body’ (2 Corinthians 4:10). And again: ‘If we endure, we shall also reign with him’ (2 Timothy 2:12). If we are conformed to his death and his sufferings, as it is written, we shall share in the resurrection and the glory as well (Philippians 3:10–11). So then Christ suffered for us outside the gate, as the blessed Paul says, and we too go out of the gate, bearing his reproach (Hebrews 13:12–13); slain in the same way, like a young calf, and burned whole like a ram, we make our life in Christ fragrant to God. These, then, are the victims offered for Aaron and for those with him and descended from him. For the people, a male goat is the sin offering (Leviticus 9:15). And why is that, when a young calf was offered for the cleansing of the priests? Everything that belongs to the priests stands higher: the bringing of sacrifices and the rites of cleansing and purification. And a young calf is larger in body than a goat, and so displays a clear token of the spiritual pre-eminence found in the realities themselves. The young calf and the lamb for the whole burnt offering (Leviticus 9:3) hint at the infancy in Christ of those consecrated in faith. The calf and the ram signify very well endurance and courage, and fruitfulness in gentleness: the calf is the type of the first, the ram of the second (Leviticus 9:4). The fine flour soaked with oil (Leviticus 9:4) shows very clearly the bright hope of the life in Christ. For it is not in gloom and tears…
